claim: Following CNS demyelination, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) are able to differentiate into either remyelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs) or remyelinating Schwann cells (SCs).
source: Following CNS demyelination, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) are able to differentiate into either remyelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs) or remyelinating Schwann cells (SCs).
evidence: This is supported by previous research cited in the manuscript and is a foundational premise of the study.

claim: An ectopic, injury-induced perivascular niche is enriched with secreted ligands of the BMP and Wnt signalling pathways, produced by activated OPCs and endothelium.
source: By comparative transcriptome profiling we demonstrate that an ectopic, injury-induced perivascular niche is enriched with secreted ligands of the BMP and Wnt signalling pathways, produced by activated OPCs and endothelium
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome profiling data presented in the manuscript, including microarray analysis and in situ hybridization results.

claim: Reactive astrocytes within non-vascular area express the dual BMP/Wnt antagonist Sostdc1.
source: whereas reactive astrocyte within non-vascular area express the dual BMP/Wnt antagonist Sostdc1.
evidence: This is demonstrated through in situ hybridization and immunostaining showing Sostdc1 expression in astrocytes in non-vascular areas.

claim: The balance of BMP/Wnt signalling network is instructive for OPCs to undertake fate decision shortly after their activation.
source: The balance of BMP/Wnt signalling network is instructive for OPCs to undertake fate decision shortly after their activation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing differential expression of BMP and Wnt ligands and their antagonists in different niches, and functional experiments with inhibitors.

claim: Disruption of the OPCs homeostasis during demyelination results in BMP4 upregulation, which, in the absence of Sostdc1, favours SCs differentiation.
source: disruption of the OPCs homeostasis during demyelination results in BMP4 upregulation, which, in the absence of Socstdc1, favours SCs differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data showing BMP4 upregulation in vascular niches where Sostdc1 is absent, and by transplantation experiments.

claim: The contribution of SCs to CNS remyelination have been reported in several clinical conditions including traumatic spinal cord injury, leukodystrophies, and most frequently in severe forms of multiple sclerosis.
source: The contribution of SCs to CNS remyelination have been reported in several clinical conditions including traumatic spinal cord injury, leukodystrophies (Bunge et al., 1993; Guest et al., 2005), and most frequently in severe forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) (Itoyama et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: SC-mediated remyelination has been observed following virtually all forms of CNS injury with a demyelinating component, including ischemic, excitotoxic, and traumatic injury as well as in toxic and immune-mediated models of demyelination.
source: Experimentally, this phenomenon has been observed following virtually all forms of CNS injury with a demyelinating component, including ischemic, excitotoxic, and traumatic injury as well as in toxic and immune-mediated models of demyelination (Snyder et al., 1975; Dusart et al., 1992; Felts et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: It was originally assumed that SCs invaded demyelinated regions of the CNS from the periphery following a breach in the glia limitans.
source: It was originally assumed that SCs invaded demyelinated regions of the CNS from the periphery following a breach in the glia limitans (for review see Franklin and Blakemore, 1993).
evidence: This is a historical perspective cited from previous literature.

claim: Following CNS demyelination, adult OPCs are presented with a fate choice, having the option to become OLs or SCs as they contribute to remyelination.
source: However, we have previously shown using a genetic fate mapping strategy that following CNS demyelination, adult OPCs are presented with a fate choice, having the option to become OLs or SCs as they contribute to remyelination (Zawadzka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors using genetic fate mapping.

claim: Assinck et al., 2017 demonstrated extensive Schwann cell-mediated remyelination following clinically relevant traumatic spinal contusion injury and provided confirmatory evidence for their central origin using genetic reporters.
source: Recently, Assinck et al., 2017 demonstrated extensive Schwann cell-mediated remyelination following clinically relevant traumatic spinal contusion injury and using genetic reporters provided confirmatory evidence for their central origin.
evidence: This is a citation to recent confirmatory work by other researchers.

claim: SCs can be predominantly found in the CNS areas from which astrocytes are absent.
source: We and others have reported that SCs can be predominantly found in the CNS areas from which astrocytes are absent (Woodruff and Franklin, 1999; Blakemore, 1975; Blakemore, 2005; Talbott et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The central role of astrocytes in determining which type of remyelination occurs has been demonstrated by increased SCs remyelination when the astrocyte response to demyelination has been reduced either transgenically or by reducing testosterone signalling.
source: The central role of astrocytes in determining which type of remyelination occurs has recently been demonstrated by increased SCs remyelination when the astrocyte response to demyelination has been reduced either transgenically (Monteiro de Castro et al., 2015) or by reducing testosterone signalling (Bielecki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent experimental studies.

claim: Transplantation studies suggest that the molecular composition of an astrocyte-free CNS environment promotes SC differentiation of adult OPCs, possibly via a mechanism that involves bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).
source: Transplantation studies suggest that the molecular composition of an astrocyte-free CNS environment promotes SC differentiation of adult OPCs, possibly via a mechanism that involves bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) (Talbott et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on cited transplantation studies.

claim: BMPs primarily promote OPC differentiation into astrocytes in vivo.
source: However, BMPs alone are unlikely to induce SC differentiation since they primarily promote OPC differentiation into astrocytes in vivo (Mabie et al., 1997; Grinspan et al., 2000; Gomes et al., 2003; Cheng et al., 2007; Sabo et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: BMPs promote astrocyte and neuronal fate in vitro.
source: or astrocyte and neuronal fate in vitro (Kondo and Raff, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to in vitro studies.

claim: Fate decisions by adult multipotential cells are often regulated by a specialized microenvironment, termed the 'niche', associated with the vasculature.
source: Fate decisions by adult multipotential cells are often regulated by a specialized microenvironment, termed the 'niche', associated with the vasculature (Goldman and Chen, 2011).
evidence: This is a general principle supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Injury-induced loss of the local vasculature and disruption of blood brain barrier (BBB) integrity is a common pathological feature of demyelinating disease.
source: Injury-induced loss of the local vasculature and disruption of blood brain barrier (BBB) integrity is a common pathological feature of demyelinating disease
evidence: This is established knowledge about demyelinating disease pathology.

claim: Tissue reconstruction is associated with enhanced angiogenesis and the reestablishment of a functional vasculature.
source: while tissue reconstruction is associated with enhanced angiogenesis and the reestablishment of a functional vasculature (Miyamoto et al., 2014; Egawa et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Unique properties of the perivascular niche within remyelinating white matter would create microenvironment that favour the alternative differentiation of OPCs.
source: We hypothesized that unique properties of the perivascular niche within remyelinating white matter would create microenvironment that favour the alternative differentiation of OPCs.
evidence: This is the central hypothesis of the study.

claim: Toxin injection results in focal primary demyelination lesion with large astrocyte-deficient areas and little axonal loss.
source: Toxin injection results in focal primary demyelination lesion (Figure 1A) with large astrocyte-deficient areas and little axonal loss.
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the experimental model used, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The CCP is anatomically remote from spinal root transition zones, which are potential sources of cells of neural crest origin such as SCs or boundary cap cells.
source: The CCP is anatomically remote from spinal root transition zones, which are potential sources of cells of neural crest origin such as SCs or boundary cap cells (Fraher, 1992; Zujovic et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an anatomical fact supported by citations.

claim: Numerous Olig2+ cells were preferentially associated with blood vessels and reached their highest density in the VN at 10 days post-lesion induction (dpl).
source: Numerous Olig2+ cells were preferentially associated with blood vessels and reached their highest density in the VN at 10 days post-lesion induction (dpl) (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: The vast majority of Olig2+ cells co-expressed the oligodendrocyte lineage transcription factor Sox10 and Sox2.
source: The vast majority of these cells co-expressed the oligodendrocyte lineage transcription factor Sox10 (Hornig et al., 2013) and Sox2, a transcription factor associated with OPC activation and early stages of differentiation (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical data and supported by citations.

claim: From 10 dpl there was a significant increase of the number of cells Sox10+/Sox2+ but that were Olig2-.
source: From 10 dpl there was a significant increase of the number of cells Sox10+/Sox2+ but that were Olig2- (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: By 14 dpl up to 80% of total Sox10+ within the VN were Olig2-.
source: By 14 dpl up to 80% of total Sox10+ within the VN were Olig2- (av. 68.40 ± 14.65%, Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Sox10 is a transcription factor required for both OLs and SCs homeostasis and myelin maintenance.
source: Since Sox10 is a transcription factor required for both OLs and SCs homeostasis and myelin maintenance (Bremer et al., 2011)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Downregulation of Olig2 expression might be associated with switch in differentiation program and Olig2-/Sox10+/Sox2+ cells could give rise to cells producing peripheral-type myelin.
source: we hypothesized that downregulation of Olig2 expression might be associated with switch in differentiation program and Olig2-/Sox10+/Sox2+ cells could give rise to cells producing peripheral-type myelin.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed data.

claim: No significant differences in the number of apoptotic OPCs between the VN and non-vascular regions at any time points investigated.
source: To rule out cell death as the cause of the decrease in Olig2+ cells within the VN we performed immunohistochemistry for activated caspase three and found no significant differences in the number of apoptotic OPCs between the VN and non-vascular regions at any time points investigated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Olig2-/Sox10+ cells at 14 dpl in the VN were likely of OPC origin.
source: Using Pdgfra-Cre reporter mice, we found that the Olig2-/Sox10+ cells at 14 dpl in the VN were likely of OPC origin (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by genetic fate mapping data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells can lose Olig2 expression at early stages of differentiation while continuing to express Sox10 and Sox2.
source: These data suggest that oligodendrocyte lineage cells can lose Olig2 expression at early stages of differentiation while continuing to express Sox10 and Sox2
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Cells clustered within the VN are a source of SCs that eventually remyelinate the VN axons.
source: and that these cells, clustered within the VN are a source of SCs that eventually remyelinate the VN axons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed cell phenotypes and locations.

claim: Substantial regeneration of blood vessels and BBB within the areas undergoing remyelination occurred in parallel with remyelination.
source: We also found substantial regeneration of blood vessels and BBB within the areas undergoing remyelination. Blood vessels rebuilding their basement membrane and endothelial walls occurred in parallel with remyelination (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Perivascular SCs formed a network by contacting each other with no discontinuity of basement membrane of the wall of blood vessels and such capillaries rebuild BBB.
source: Of note, perivascular SCs formed a network by contacting each other with no discontinuity of basement membrane of the wall of blood vessels and such capillaries rebuild BBB (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Strong signal from MPZ mRNA only occurred in cells closely associated with the vasculature.
source: Strong signal from MPZ mRNA only occurred in cells closely associated with the vasculature, suggesting that an interaction between progenitors and blood vessels might be necessary for their alternative, SC differentiation (Figure 1E,I).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E,I.

claim: Transcripts for MPZ and PLP were mutually exclusive and spatially separated.
source: Double ISH revealed that transcripts for MPZ and PLP (encoding an oligodendrocyte specific protein) were mutually exclusive and spatially separated (Figure 2E,II).
evidence: This is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2E,II.

claim: MPZ and PLP segregation was clearly detectable among cells expressed Sox10 in defined areas within remyelinated CNS lesions.
source: Moreover, MPZ and PLP segregation was also clearly detectable among cells expressed Sox10 in defined areas within remyelinated CNS lesions (Figure 2E,III).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2E,III.

claim: Periaxin+ SCs preferentially occupy discrete areas where astrocytes were absent even around the same vessel.
source: Close examination of the VN revealed that periaxin+ SCs preferentially occupy discrete areas where astrocytes were absent even around the same vessel (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Blood vessel itself or blood vessel-created microenvironment together with astrocyte absence are critical determinants for specific OPCs differentiation.
source: Our observations suggest that blood vessel itself or blood vessel-created microenvironment together with astrocyte absence are critical determinants for specific OPCs differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation and conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: 115 genes with significantly changed expression in the VN between 6 and 10 dpl, and 313 genes with significantly changed expression in non-VN.
source: We found 115 genes with significantly changed expression in the VN between 6 and 10 dpl, and 313 genes with significantly changed expression in non-VN (adj.p-values<0.05; the source data are summarized in Figure 2—source data 1–3).
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis data.

claim: Within genes upregulated in the VN we found several transcripts strongly associated with the endothelium.
source: Within genes upregulated in the VN we found several transcripts strongly associated with the endothelium.
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis and comparison with known endothelial gene signatures.

claim: The non-VN was enriched in several known astrocyte transcripts.
source: In contrast, the non-VN was enriched in several known astrocyte transcripts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis and comparison with known astrocyte gene signatures, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Significant differences between the two area-specific transcriptomes only at 10 dpl, which suggested that the majority of molecular events determining OPC differentiation take place around this time.
source: We observed significant differences between the two area-specific transcriptomes only at 10 dpl, which suggested that the majority of molecular events determining OPC differentiation take place around this time.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the microarray data showing temporal differences.

claim: Ascl2 and Sox9, coding for transcription factors previously implicated in SC differentiation programme, significantly upregulated in the VN.
source: Among differentially expressed genes we found Ascl2 and Sox9, coding for transcription factors previously implicated in SC differentiation programme (Küry et al., 2002; Weider and Wegner, 2017), significantly upregulated in the VN (Figure 2C, FC=1.33, FC=1.27, respectively, adj.pv<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2C and citations to previous research.

claim: Sox10 was stably expressed within the VN.
source: We also examined expression of Sox10, critically required for myelination in both CNS and PNS (Hornig et al., 2013; Vogl et al., 2013) and found it stably expressed within the VN (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2C and citations.

claim: Several genes encoding for extracellular matrix proteins (ECM; dystroglycan 1, Dag1; collagen type V alpha 3, Col5a3; cell adhesion molecule 4, Cadm4) were significantly upregulated within the VN at 10 dpl.
source: In addition, several genes encoding for extracellular matrix proteins (ECM; dystroglycan 1, Dag1; collagen type V alpha 3, Col5a3; cell adhesion molecule 4, Cadm4) were significantly upregulated within the VN at 10 dpl.
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis data.

claim: The distinctive VN transcriptome might be required for SC differentiation.
source: These data suggested that the distinctive VN transcriptome might be required for SC differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed transcriptome differences.

claim: BMP acts as a negative regulator of OL differentiation by preventing cell mobilization and maturation and promotion of astrogliosis.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that BMP acts as a negative regulator of OL differentiation by preventing cell mobilization and maturation and promotion of astrogliosis.
evidence: This is a summary of previous research findings cited in the manuscript.

claim: BMP4 was identified as an OPCs-derived factor whose increased expression in the VN did not correlate with astrogenesis.
source: We identified BMP4 as an OPCs-derived factor whose increased expression in the VN did not, however, correlate with astrogenesis.
evidence: This is based on the microarray data and in situ hybridization showing BMP4 expression in OPCs.

claim: Adult OPCs do not differentiate significantly into astrocytes in vivo, only occasionally OPC-derived astrocytes were found in the non-vascular areas.
source: Moreover, as we showed previously, adult OPCs do not differentiate significantly into astrocytes in vivo, only occasionally we found OPC-derived astrocytes in the non-vascular areas (Zawadzka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors.

claim: BMP4 takes part in the autonomous, alternative PNS-like, OPC differentiation.
source: Our results suggest that BMP4 takes part in the autonomous, alternative PNS-like, OPC differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: BMP4 has been proposed to promote differentiation of engrafted adult OPCs primarily into cells with immunophenotypic and ultrastructural characteristics of myelinating SCs.
source: BMP4 has been proposed to promote differentiation of engrafted adult OPCs primarily into cells with immunophenotypic and ultrastructural characteristics of myelinating SCs (Talbott et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on cited transplantation studies.

claim: SC differentiation was blocked when OPCs were co-transplanted with astrocytes or by noggin overexpression in engrafted OPCs.
source: SC differentiation was blocked when OPCs were co-transplanted with astrocytes or by noggin overexpression in engrafted OPCs.
evidence: This is based on cited transplantation studies.

claim: Neither noggin overexpression nor the presence of co-transplanted astrocytes enhanced differentiation into OLs, suggesting that suppression of BMP signalling alone is not sufficient to promote OL differentiation.
source: However, neither noggin overexpression nor the presence of co-transplanted astrocytes enhanced differentiation into OLs, suggesting that suppression of BMP signalling alone is not sufficient to promote OL differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of cited transplantation studies.

claim: Endogenous OL remyelination is normally successful in the perimeter of lesions, coinciding with a region of densely populated reactive astrocytes.
source: Since endogenous OL remyelination is normally successful in the perimeter of lesions, coinciding with a region of densely populated reactive astrocytes (Blakemore and Crang, 1989; Franklin and Blakemore, 1993; Talbott et al., 2006)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: BMP4 is necessary but not sufficient to induce PNS-like differentiation program.
source: Our results suggest that BMP4 is necessary but not sufficient to induce PNS-like differentiation program.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Upon demyelination OPCs upregulate BMP4 and loose Sosctdc1 expression which enable them to convert into activated cells, primed for differentiation.
source: Upon demyelination OPCs upregulate BMP4 and loose Sosctdc1 expression which enable them to convert into activated cells, primed for differentiation.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data showing BMP4 upregulation in OPCs and absence of Sostdc1 in the vascular niche.

claim: BMP4 treatment inhibits the progression of OPC differentiation toward OLs by favouring global histone acetylation and nuclear chromatin conformation characteristic for euchromatin.
source: In particular, it has been shown that BMP4 treatment inhibits the progression of OPC differentiation toward OLs by favouring global histone acetylation and nuclear chromatin conformation characteristic for euchromatin.
evidence: This is based on cited previous studies.

claim: BMP4 acts as a potent inducer of gene expression, possibly supporting the undifferentiated progenitor state and/or making the cells more responsive to the other signals such as Wnt.
source: Thus, BMP4 acts as a potent inducer of gene expression, possibly supporting the undifferentiated progenitor state and/or making the cells more responsive to the other signals such as Wnt.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on cited studies and the current findings.

claim: OL differentiation is accompanied by peripheral chromatin condensation in OPCs and decrease in histone deacetylation at transcriptional repressors of oligodendrocytic differentiation such as Sox11 and Sox2.
source: In contrast, OL differentiation is accompanied by peripheral chromatin condensation in OPCs (Wu et al., 2012) and decrease in histone deacetylation at transcriptional repressors of oligodendrocytic differentiation such as Sox11 (He et al., 2007) and Sox2 (Lyssiotis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on cited previous studies.

claim: BMP4 expression coincides with OPCs activation and this provides an additional aspect to the notion that OPCs can acquire multipotency in specific conditions of local microenvironment.
source: We show that BMP4 expression coincides with OPCs activation and this provides an additional aspect to the notion that OPCs can acquire multipotency in specific conditions of local microenvironment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Astrocyte-derived Sostdc1 controls biological availability of BMP4 in the non-vascular area and maintains OL-driven remyelination.
source: Consequently, astrocyte-derived Sostdc1 controls biological availability of BMP4 in the non-vascular area and maintains OL-driven remyelination.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the expression patterns of BMP4 and Sostdc1.

claim: Sostdc1 is produced exclusively by activated astrocytes within the non-VN lesion area during the period of first 10 days post demyelination.
source: Since Sostdc1 is produced exclusively by activated astrocytes within the non-VN lesion area during the period of first 10 days post demyelination
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and immunostaining data.

claim: Astrocytes are one of the key regulators of OPC differentiation fate.
source: our data corroborate with the long-postulated notion that astrocytes are one of the key regulators of OPC differentiation fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and previous literature.

claim: OPCs can generate SCs cells in the PNS under the condition resembling the CNS perivascular niche, in a BMP and Wnt dependent manner.
source: Our in vivo experiments provide evidence for the ability of OPCs to generate SCs cells in the PNS under the condition resembling the CNS perivascular niche, in a BMP and Wnt dependent manner.
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments with pharmacological and genetic manipulations.

claim: OPC differentiation was affected by both USAG1 and dorsomorphin treatment.
source: OPC differentiation was affected by both USAG1 and dorsomorphin treatment.
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: USAG1 binds directly to BMPs and antagonizes BMP signalling and interacts with the LRP6 receptor to antagonize Wnt signalling.
source: USAG1 (a product of human ortholog of rat gene sostdc1) binds directly to BMPs and antagonizes BMP signalling (Yanagita et al., 2006) and interacts with the LRP6 receptor to antagonize Wnt signalling (Lintern et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dorsomorphin is a potent inhibitor of BMP signalling which binds to the BMP type I receptors ALK1/2/3/6 and type II receptor ActRIIA.
source: Dorsomorphin is a potent inhibitor of BMP signalling which binds to the BMP type I receptors ALK1/2/3/6 and type II receptor ActRIIA (Horbelt et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: BMP stimulation seems to be indispensable for the alternative fate induction.
source: Thus, BMP stimulation seems to be indispensable for the alternative fate induction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transplantation experiments with BMP inhibitors.

claim: Inhibition of Lrp6-dependent Wnt signaling prevents OPC-to-SC differentiation even within the high BMP4 background of injured sciatic nerve.
source: Moreover, inhibition of Lrp6-dependent Wnt signaling prevents OPC-to-SC differentiation even within the high BMP4 background of injured sciatic nerve.
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments with LRP6 shRNA shown in Figure 6.

claim: Activation of WNT signalling is required for initiation of PNS fate differentiation.
source: Defective phenotype of cells transduced with LRP6 shRNA indicates that activation of WNT signalling is required for initiation of PNS fate differentiation which has not been proposed yet.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the LRP6 knockdown experiments.

claim: OPCs differentiate into SCs when exposed to BMP/Wnt-enriched PNS environment; however, an axonal contact seems to be an indispensable factor.
source: Our findings demonstrate that OPCs differentiate into SCs when exposed to BMP/Wnt-enriched PNS environment; however, an axonal contact seems to be an indispensable factor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transplantation experiments.

claim: Neuregulin-1 (Nrg1) mediates SCs remyelination by precursors of CNS origin after spinal cord injury.
source: This is consistent with recent findings showing that neuregulin-1 (Nrg1) mediates SCs remyelination by precursors of CNS origin after spinal cord injury (Bartus et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on cited recent research.

claim: While neuregulin-1 is evidently important for Schwann cell myelination of the CNS axons, there is no evidence in the whole genome analysis to suggest that Ngr1 is involved in OPCs fate determination at its early stage.
source: However, while neuregulin-1 is evidently important for Schwann cell myelination of the CNS axons, we did not find any evidence in our whole genome analysis to suggest that Ngr1 is involved in OPCs fate determination at its early stage.
evidence: This is based on the microarray analysis results.

claim: CNS-derived SCs substantially differ from PNS myelinating cells by different CTGF production.
source: by using a transgenic approach we have provided novel evidence that CNS-derived SCs substantially differ from PNS myelinating cells, that is by different CTGF production.
evidence: This is based on experiments using Wnt1-Cre mice shown in Figure 7.

claim: CTGF participates in the pathological reaction of the astrocytic compartment.
source: We show that CTGF participates in the pathological reaction of the astrocytic compartment which is in line with previous reports describing contribution of accumulating CTGF+ astrocytes to wound healing and glial scar formation in response traumatic brain injury (Hertel et al., 2000).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data and supported by citation.

claim: This study is the first to demonstrate the PNS-like OPC differentiation effect of BMP and Wnt signalling, both of which are signalling pathways associated with inhibition of OL differentiation and maturation.
source: This study is the first to demonstrate the PNS-like OPC differentiation effect of BMP and Wnt signalling, both of which are signalling pathways associated with inhibition of OL differentiation and maturation.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the novel findings.

claim: BMPs induce OPC priming and activation and, when combined with Wnt, instruct them to differentiate into peripheral myelin producing cells.
source: We propose that BMPs induce OPC priming and activation and, when combined with Wnt, instruct them to differentiate into peripheral myelin producing cells.
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Bmp4 and Wnt2 transcripts but not Sostdc1 were significantly increased early after sciatic nerve injury.
source: We found that Bmp4 and Wnt2 transcripts but not Sostdc1 were significantly increased early after sciatic nerve injury (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: GFP+ cells implanted at 24 hr after injury were broadly distributed around the injection place and displayed distinctive morphology typical for PNS-type SCs, positive for periaxin, formed a 1:1 association with axons, and clear organization of internodes.
source: GFP+ cells implanted at 24 hr after injury were broadly distributed around the injection place and displayed distinctive morphology typical for PNS-type SCs, positive for periaxin, a protein occurring only in PNS-myelin, formed a 1:1 association with axons, and clear organization of internodes (74.7 ± 10.25% of GFP+ cells, Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments and immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Cells pre-treated and injected in the presence of dorsomorphin were present in recipient nerves, but they rarely produced peripheral myelin protein and did not formed the myelin sheaths.
source: The cells pre-treated and injected in the presence of dorsomorphin were present in recipient nerves, but they rarely produced peripheral myelin protein and did not formed the myelin sheaths (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: USAG-pretreated OPCs were present close to the injection site, formed an irregular mesh, rarely contacted with an individual axon to form myelin sheath and produced periaxin.
source: Many patches of GFP+ cells were found also in sciatic nerves injected with USAG-pretreted OPCs: however, they were present close to the injection site, formed an irregular mesh, rarely contacted with an individual axon to form myelin sheath and produced periaxin (Figure 5B,C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5B,C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Untreated cells implanted at three dpc did not produce periaxin after 28 dpc and did not produce GFAP or Olig2.
source: In contrast to OPCs grafted into sciatic nerves at 24 hr after crush, untreated cells implanted at three dpc did not produce periaxin after 28 dpc. Also, they did not produce GFAP, normally expressed by astrocytes in CNS and non-myelinating SCs in the PNS as well as they lost the expression of Olig2, constitutively expressed by oligodendrocyte lineage cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: OPCs were highly proliferative when transplanted to the sciatic nerve at 3 and 6 dpc and the cells populated large areas of the nerve.
source: OPCs were highly proliferative when transplanted to the sciatic nerve at 3 and 6 dpc and the cells populated large areas of the nerve (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Efficacy of gene expression silencing at the protein level by LRP6 shRNA was 73 ± 4.3% compared to non-targeting control shRNA-transduced cells.
source: We determined efficacy of gene expression silencing at the protein level by densitometry of western blot signals in OPCs as 73 ± 4,3% compared to non-targeting control shRNA-transduced cells (mean ±SEM of two experiments, Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Transduced cells differentiated normally into MBP-produced oligodendrocytes at 6 div in differentiation medium.
source: Transduced cells differentiated normally into MBP-produced oligodendrocytes at 6 div in differentiation medium (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on in vitro differentiation experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Only control non-targeting shRNA-transduced GFP+/tRFP+ cells showed typical morphology of MPZ-producing Schwann cells within host sciatic nerves.
source: However, only control non-targeting shRNA-transduced GFP+/tRFP+ cells showed typical morphology of MPZ-producing Schwann cells within host sciatic nerves.
evidence: This is based on transplantation experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Schwann cell differentiation of LRP6 shRNA lentiviral transduced OPCs was significantly impaired; only 15.8 ± 12% of GFP+ cells were periaxin-positive in contrast to the control shRNA-transduced cells (73.6 ± 16.9% differentiated into Schwann cells).
source: For quantification we detected intracellular Schwann cell protein, periaxin and demonstrated that Schwann cell differentiation of LRP6 shRNA lentiviral transduced OPCs was significantly impaired; only 15.8 ± 12% of GFP+ cells were periaxin-positive in contrast to the control shRNA-transduced cells (73.6 ± 16.9% differentiated into Schwann cells).
evidence: This is based on quantification of transplantation experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of Wnt signaling inhibited Schwann cell differentiation of OPC within injured sciatic nerve suggesting a key role of Wnt in cell differentiation decision.
source: Thus, we found that pharmacological or genetic inhibition of Wnt signaling inhibited Schwann cell differentiation of OPC within injured sciatic nerve suggesting a key role of Wnt in cell differentiation decision.

claim: Activation of both BMP and Wnt signalling might be required for initiation of OPC alternative differentiation.
source: These results suggest that activation of both BMP and Wnt signalling might be required for initiation of OPC alternative differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transplantation experiments.

claim: Genes encoding for collagens (Col5a3, Col11a1, Col1a2) were the most substantially upregulated extracellular matrix proteins in the VN.
source: The extracellular matrix proteins were the second functional group of genes found to be specifically enriched in the VN and the most substantially upregulated being genes encoding for collagens (Col5a3, Col11a1, Col1a2) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Within non-VN there was increased expression of vimentin (Vtn) and fibronectin (Fn1).
source: In contrast, within non-VN there was increased expression of vimentin (Vtn) and fibronectin (Fn1).

claim: A particularly highly expressed gene within the non-VN was connective tissue growth factor (CTGF).
source: A particularly highly expressed gene within the non-VN was connective tissue growth factor (CTGF).
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis.

claim: CTGF can bind multiple ligands and interact with many other proteins in the remodeling of lesion environments.
source: CTGF, a member of the CCN family of secreted matricellular proteins, can bind multiple ligands and interact with many other proteins in the remodeling of lesion environments.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CTGF function.

claim: CTGF interactions with the ECM and integrins have been reported to affect oligodendrocyte differentiation.
source: Its interactions with the ECM and integrins have been reported to affect oligodendrocyte differentiation (Colognato et al., 2002).
evidence: This is based on cited previous research.

claim: CTGF has been recently identified as a SC-derived factor inhibitory for myelination.
source: Moreover, CTGF has been recently identified as a SC-derived factor inhibitory for myelination (Lamond and Barnett, 2013).
evidence: This is based on cited recent research.

claim: CTGF expression decreased gradually during CNS remyelination, with expression levels consistently lower in the VN than in non-VN.

claim: The lowest expression of CTGF was detected in VN at 14 dpl, when the first mature SCs were already present in the niche.
source: The lowest expression of CTGF was detected in VN at 14 dpl, when the first mature SCs were already present in the niche.

claim: Very few MPZ+/YFP+ SCs were detected within the lesions at 28 dpl in Wnt1-Cre mice, even if the lesion was located next to the ventral root.

claim: MPZ+ myelin within the CNS lesion was almost exclusively associated with cells negative for YFP.

claim: Cells that remyelinated spinal cord white matter did not produce CTGF.

claim: CTGF+ cells were mainly detected at the lesion rim and displayed the typical stellate morphology of activated astrocytes.
source: The CTGF+ cells were mainly detected at the lesion rim and displayed the typical stellate morphology of activated astrocytes (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Expression and accumulation of CTGF is restricted to the astrocytic response to demyelination.
source: These findings strongly suggest that expression and accumulation of CTGF is restricted to the astrocytic response to demyelination.

claim: Mature CNS-derived SCs differ from their PNS counterparts that supports the previously postulated similarity between them and OLs rather than bona fide PNS glia.

claim: CNS-derived SCs selectively occupied the perivascular area devoid of astrocytes.

claim: Differentiation of OPCs into SCs depends, at least partially, on vascular reorganization.

claim: The tissue around the blood vessels promotes preferential accumulation of activated OPCs early after demyelinating insult, which correlates with remodelling of the capillary network.
source: We show that the tissue around the blood vessels promotes preferential accumulation of activated OPCs early after demyelinating insult, which correlates with remodelling of the capillary network.

claim: Cerebral endothelium promote OPC migration along blood vessels during development.
